title: Teaching Large Language Models to Self-Debug
abstract: This work proposes a novel approach called S ELF -D EBUGGING, which teaches large language models to debug their predicted code via few-shot demonstrations. The model learns to identify mistakes by investigating execution results and explaining the generated code in natural language, achieving state-of-the-art performance on several code generation benchmarks.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content: Imagine you're a programmer trying to write a complex code. You wouldn't just write it once and hope it's correct. Instead, you'd write, test, and debug it iteratively. Self-debugging is a similar process for large language models, where they learn to identify mistakes by explaining their generated code and investigating execution results. This approach is reminiscent of rubber duck debugging, where explaining code line-by-line to a rubber duck helps human programmers debug more efficiently.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content: The S ELF -D EBUGGING process involves three main steps: Generation, Explanation, and Feedback. The model generates code, explains it, and then uses the explanation and execution results to generate feedback. This feedback is used to improve the code in the next iteration. We use few-shot prompting to instruct the model to perform these steps.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content: We evaluate S ELF -D EBUGGING on several code generation benchmarks, including Spider for text-to-SQL generation, TransCoder for code translation, and MBPP for text-to-Python generation. Our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance, with improvements of up to 12% on some benchmarks.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content: S ELF -D EBUGGING has significant implications for code generation and program repair. By teaching large language models to self-debug, we can improve their coding capabilities and reduce the sampling cost required to accomplish challenging tasks. This approach also has potential applications in natural language processing and reasoning.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content: The key innovation of S ELF -D EBUGGING is the use of few-shot prompting to instruct the model to perform self-debugging. This approach allows the model to learn from its own mistakes and improve its coding capabilities without requiring additional training data or human feedback.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content: To try S ELF -D EBUGGING yourself, you can use a large language model like code-davinci-002 or gpt-3.5-turbo. Simply provide a problem description, generate code, and then use the self-debugging process to improve the code. You can also experiment with different prompting techniques and feedback formats to see what works best for your use case.
